course_name_original: Aprovechamiento Energético de Recursos Hidráulicos y Eólicos
course_name_en: Energy Exploitation of Hydraulic and Wind Resources

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
Achieving the ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

Autonomous learning ability that allows continued study through the development of the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Ability to identify, analyze and assess the dominant basic phenomena in fluid mechanical processes and energy transfer and utilization in engineering and industry.
Fundamental analysis of fluid mechanical and thermal problems of interest in the energy industry, identifying strong and weak variables and evaluating possible simplifying hypotheses.
Performance of elemental calculations for sizing, selection of machines and equipment, and operation for fluid installations with energy transfers.
Ability to study, propose, and apply different types of technologies to improve the utilization and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs.
Knowledge of the advances and latest trends on the general equipment and operating characteristics of hydraulic and wind power plants.
Apply the principles of hydraulic and wind renewable energy conversion in a reasoned way.
Evaluate the hydraulic and/or wind resources available in a given area or environment.
Work on practical cases of general design, basic equipment sizing, modeling, analysis, and regulation of hydraulic power plants and wind farms.
Know and apply the operation and management strategies of hydraulic and wind resource conversion plants.

syllabus_topics: Types of hydraulic exploitations, equipment, and operation strategies.
Infrastructures and equipment for hydraulic power plants.
Types, performance, and operation of hydraulic turbines.
Types, performance, and operation of wind turbines.
Planning and management of wind farms.

assessment_methods.method: Activities in laboratory practicals and site visits (results sheet delivery)
Activities in classroom practicals (results sheet delivery)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is 40% from the final exam and 60% from practical activities. The practical activities include laboratory work/site visits and classroom practicals, each contributing 30%. To pass, a non-zero score must be obtained in each block of exercises and questions on the exam, and a minimum of 4 out of 10 points must be achieved on the exam itself in the ordinary call. In extraordinary calls, the exam accounts for 100% of the final grade. Notes from practical classes are valid for the ordinary call of the current academic year.
